validity.researcher_notes: This is one of the most extensively, independently documented pipeline proposals in the whole India-gas cluster -- not remotely a GEM-only/phantom entity. Starting from the sheet's own wiki citations (hydrocarbons-technology.com -- now redirects to offshore-technology.com/projects/iran-pipeline/ -- economictimes 2017, upi.com 2010, oilprice.com 2017), all four still resolve live, and I corroborated them with additional independent primary/secondary sources found via open search: gulfoilandgas.com's dated project-timeline page (2700 km, South Pars->Karachi/Multan->Delhi route, USD 7.5bn agreement, extensive 2002-2011 milestone log), dawn.com (Pakistan's national English daily), openthemagazine.com (India), and insightsonindia.com (a March 2026 explainer, the most current evidence I could find). Existence: unambiguous -- this was a real, formally negotiated trilateral state-to-state project (Iran's NIGEC and Pakistan's Interstate Gas Systems signed a bilateral implementation agreement in Istanbul on 5 June 2009 after India's exit), not a rumor or a GEM invention. Classification: correctly recorded as a gas transmission trunk line (a 2700 km international cross-border trunk from a production hub to demand centers), not a gathering/feeder/CGD line -- no classification concern. Duplicate check against the roster: none of the other 12 India-gas rows (all domestic West Bengal/Rajasthan/Andhra corridors) geographically or conceptually overlaps P0451's Iran->Pakistan->India route, so no duplicate/relabel risk within this batch. IMPORTANT ADJACENT-ENTITY NOTE (not a duplicate, but worth flagging for whoever next touches Iran or Pakistan gas): GEM also carries a separate wiki page/ProjectID for 'Iran-Pakistan Pipeline' (the bilateral, India-less successor that Iran and Pakistan pursued after 2009 and that Iran mostly built on its own side by ~2012-2013). That is a genuinely distinct entity from P0451 -- P0451 correctly represents the abandoned trilateral concept with India as the third leg/purchaser, while the other entity represents the still-nominally-alive Iran-Pakistan bilateral line. They should NOT be merged; they are out of scope for this India-gas batch (that other row would live in an Iran or Pakistan gas batch), but I flag the relationship here because a careless future pass could mistake P0451's cancellation for evidence the bilateral pipe never existed, which is wrong -- Iran did build most of its own side. Precision note on WHICH leg is cancelled (per the sweep brief's warning about being precise here): P0451's Status=cancelled correctly applies to the India-inclusive trilateral vision / India's own participation, not to Iran-Pakistan bilateral construction, which is a separate, still-technically-live authorization not tracked under this ProjectID.

NIGEC is a real, well-known subsidiary of the National Iranian Gas Company, which does sit under Iran's Ministry of Petroleum -- so 'Iran Ministry of Petroleum' as a high-level parent label is plausible/defensible as a simplification, but it is not the entity actually named as project counterparty in the sources I could verify, so I'm not certifying it as sourced. For 'Pasargad Energy Development Co' (Owner2, 0% listed / no percent given in the worklist units besides the name) -- this is a real Iranian E&P/engineering company (pedc.ir / pasargadep.com), so the name is not fabricated or nonsensical, but I found zero independent mentions connecting it specifically to the IPI/Iran-Pakistan pipeline in English-language search. This may well be correct (Iran-side EPC contractors on South Pars-adjacent infrastructure are numerous and not always covered in English trade press), but I cannot confirm it, so per standing rule 2 I am not fabricating a citation for it. Left Owner [ref] as UNRESOLVED in fills.

validity.recommendation: Flag Capacity=3884.60 MMcf/d (110 mmscmd) as scope-ambiguous rather than fully verified at the recorded (India-inclusive, Asaluyeh->New Delhi) scope; do not treat the ref I found as closing the question.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's Capacity value converts exactly to 110 million standard cubic meters per day (3884.60 MMcf/d / 35.3147 = 110.00 mmscmd, to the decimal), and I found an exact-match source: gulfoilandgas.com's project page (titled 'Iran-Pakistan-India Gas Pipeline (IPI)') states verbatim: 'The pipeline can carry 110 million cubic meters of gas a day. 50 Mln cm meets domestic needs of Iran and the remaining 60 Mln cm will go to Pakistan.' Read literally, that 110 mmscmd breakdown (50 Iran-domestic + 60 Pakistan-bound) accounts for ZERO of it going to India -- i.e., the number the source gives as 'the pipeline's' capacity may actually describe the reduced, India-less bilateral Iran-Pakistan build-out, not the original trilateral design capacity that would have included an India allocation. Other sources give materially different, and mutually inconsistent, capacity figures for what is nominally the same trilateral project: oilprice.com (Jan 2017, also cited by the sheet) says the pipeline was meant to deliver '22 million cubic meters per day of gas' from South Pars; a general open-web search turned up a commonly repeated figure of 150 mmscmd total (60 to Pakistan + 90 to India). None of these three figures (22 / 110 / 150 mmscmd) agree with each other, and only one source explicitly discusses an India-specific allocation (90 mmscmd, in the 150-total framing) -- which is not the number on the sheet. This is exactly the kind of material spec disagreement the audit brief asks not to silently pass: the sheet's Capacity number is a real, citable published figure, but I cannot confirm it represents the India-inclusive scope this ProjectID is meant to describe, and it is more likely (per the source's own text) to describe the post-India, Iran+Pakistan-only capacity. Recommend Update-track follow-up rather than accepting the ref at face value.

offshore-technology.com states plainly 'India withdrew in 2009'. dawn.com (Pakistan) independently states: 'In 2008... India signed two major agreements with the US on nuclear energy and military cooperation. As a consequence, the following year, India withdrew from the IPI project' -- i.e. 2009. Two fully independent outlets (UK/GlobalData trade press vs Pakistani national daily) both land on 2009 explicitly. CAVEAT for the record: several other sources describe a more gradual disengagement starting earlier -- gulfoilandgas.com's timeline notes India had been 'boycotting formal talks on the project since 2007 over security concerns' (as of a 3/31/2010 entry), and insightsonindia.com's 2026 explainer says 'India effectively exited negotiations in 2007'. So 2007 is when India's active participation effectively ended, while 2009 is the year multiple sources treat as the formal/final withdrawal point (and is also the year the sheet already records). I did not change CancelledYear given 2+ independent sources explicitly state 2009, but a future pass could reasonably consider whether 2007 is more accurate as 'when it became inferred-dead' -- I'm noting the tension rather than picking one silently.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: This is a CONFIRMED cancellation, not a dormancy inference -- correctly matching the sheet's existing ShelvedCancelledType=confirmed. India's exit is well-documented state action (not silence): US-nuclear-deal-driven strategic reorientation (2008), pricing disagreement (Pakistan wanted ~$4.93-7.2/mBtu vs India's ~$0.55-1/mBtu ceiling), and Balochistan security/transit-fee concerns, formalized around 2009, after which Iran and Pakistan proceeded bilaterally without India. I searched specifically for any signs of revival up to the present: a March 2017 Economic Times piece (already cited by the sheet) shows a parliamentary panel RECOMMENDING revival, which is evidence of continued non-participation, not a change; a February 2024 Pakistani cabinet approval of construction work is specific to the bilateral Iran-Pakistan pipe and does not involve India; and the most recent item I found, an insightsonindia.com explainer dated 23 March 2026 (prompted by a West Asia crisis reviving discussion of old pipeline options), explicitly describes the IPI project's status as 'Dormant/Recast' and states India has redirected its energy-security strategy toward TAPI instead, with no active IPI negotiations. No evidence anywhere of an actual Indian re-entry, a new trilateral agreement, or Indian financing/construction activity on this route at any point 2009-2026. Status=cancelled (India's leg/the trilateral vision) remains correct through the most current evidence available; this is a confirm, not stale, because the record is one of ongoing dated news coverage (not silence) consistently reaffirming India's non-participation, up through March 2026.
